feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (63.0, the best so far) used kp 3.0, kd 0.2 and base_speed 1.5 with a 0.12 m track, and all 60 trials ended off track with max_error 0.062 to 0.066 m and line_loss_events of about 1.0. Iteration 1 raised kp to 4.5 and narrowed the track to 0.10 m, and it scored lower (53.7), with the same failure pattern. So steering gain and track width did not fix the drift, and I have restored the iteration 0 controller so that only your geometry changes. If the next race shows line_loss_events falling to near 0 while max_error stays below 0.06 m for longer, keep this sensor span. If line losses persist at about 1 per run with max_error still reaching 0.06 m, the sensor span was not the limit, and the next change should be to mass or body_length, since yaw inertia is the remaining lever. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with the lower mass, return wheel_track to 0.14 m to damp the turn rate.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events drop below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom, keep sensor x = ±0.04 and try sensor_size 0.012 m to reduce blur at the sharpest bends (iteration 0 showed 1.0 line losses per run at 0.012 m).

If line losses stay at 1.0 per run with max_error still at or above 0.06 m, try mass 0.4 kg and body_length 0.10 m to cut yaw inertia further, since iteration 0 (0.7 kg) and iteration 1 (0.6 kg) both drifted off before covering the course.
If steering_oscillation exceeds 0.2 with the lower mass, return wheel_track to 0.14 m to slow the turn rate, since iteration 1 (narrow track, higher gain) showed no benefit from a faster turn.
